title: Respectful Communication, Boundaries, and Social Media

unit.title: Program Orientation, Professionalism, and Healthcare Roles

sections.learningObjectives:
- Demonstrate respectful professional communication with patients and colleagues.
- Identify appropriate professional boundaries and maintain professional relationships.
- Describe appropriate and inappropriate use of social media and electronic communication.
- Explain why protected health information (PHI) must never be shared on social media or personal devices.
- Apply strategies for separating personal and professional online presence and escalating privacy concerns.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

When you meet someone new, you say your name and what you're there to help with. It is like introducing yourself before starting a game together so everyone knows who is on the team.

### Question 2

Listening well is like catching a ball with both hands - you stop what you are doing and really pay attention so nothing gets dropped.

### Question 3

If a friend says 'please call me Alex, not Alexander,' you call them Alex. Names are about what the person likes to be called.

### Question 4

Explaining a big word in simple words is like swapping a hard riddle for an easy clue - it helps the person solve it on their own.

### Question 5

Empathy is like saying 'I see you're sad, and that makes sense' instead of 'cheer up.' It sits with the person instead of pushing the feeling away.

### Question 6

You would not call your teacher 'sweetie.' Grown-ups deserve the same respect - use their name and title unless they ask otherwise.

### Question 7

Teach-back is like asking someone to say a rule back in their own words before a game, so you know they really got it.

### Question 8

When a pot is boiling over, turning the heat down - not up - stops the mess. Calm words do the same for angry feelings.

### Question 9

When a friend gets quiet and sad, you stay quiet with them for a bit instead of talking over the feeling.

### Question 10

Answering a phone at work is like answering the door with 'Welcome to our home, I'm Sam' instead of just opening it silently.

### Question 11

If someone can't hear well, you look at them and speak clearly, maybe write it down - you don't yell at them or talk only to their friend.

### Question 12

Your body talks even when your mouth is quiet - an open, friendly body says 'I'm glad you're here.'

### Question 13

People from different families like different things - asking what someone prefers is like asking a guest if they want tea or water instead of guessing.

### Question 14

If a teammate drops the ball, you tell them quietly and help pick it up - you don't yell about it at the whole stadium.

### Question 15

Gossip is like passing a secret around the playground - the kind thing is to not pass it on.

### Question 16

Saying 'I feel crowded' works better than 'you're pushing me' - it tells your side without starting a fight.

### Question 17

Passing a message is like a relay race - the baton has to reach the right runner with nothing dropped.

### Question 18

If you don't know the answer on a test, you ask the teacher - you don't just scribble anything.

### Question 19

In a store, a cashier asks the manager for big problems instead of guessing - that's how everyone stays safe and correct.

### Question 20

You wouldn't let a student run the whole school alone - the trained grown-ups make the big calls, and the assistant gets them.

### Question 21

Sometimes a thank-you is enough - accepting a big prize can make you feel you owe that person something, and that is not fair to either of you.

### Question 22

It is like a friendly neighbor chat - you say hello and keep it short, not share your whole diary.

### Question 23

Everyone has a bubble around them - you knock before entering someone's bubble.

### Question 24

Work notes belong in the work notebook, not your home notebook - keep them separate.

### Question 25

A teacher and student stay teacher and student - some roles just don't mix with dating.

### Question 26

Sharing a tiny, helpful bit about yourself is okay - like saying you like dogs too - but not your whole life story.

### Question 27

Your personal page is like your home - you choose who comes in, and work friends stay at the office.

### Question 28

A crossing is like stepping on a line by accident; a violation is like knocking the whole fence down on purpose.

### Question 29

A teacher doesn't pick up a student's dry cleaning - some help is not part of the job.

### Question 30

You ask before giving a hug - 'Can I give you a hug?' - because touching is always the person's choice.

### Question 31

A secret stays secret even from someone's family unless the person says it is okay to share.

### Question 32

It is like keeping your school books in one bag and your toys in another - things stay tidy and clear.

### Question 33

You don't get paid tips for being kind to a patient - kindness is part of the job.

### Question 34

A secret is a secret even if you don't say whose secret it is - you still don't tell it.

### Question 35

Before sharing a class photo, you check no one's private stuff is in the picture.

### Question 36

Every game has a rulebook - at work, the rulebook for posting is the office policy.

### Question 37

Even if you change a story, telling a friend's private business is still not okay.

### Question 38

Your work locker is for work things; your home locker is for home things - don't mix them.

### Question 39

Important secrets travel in a locked box, not on a sticky note anyone could read.

### Question 40

You can say no thanks to joining a club without a big speech - a quiet no is fine.

### Question 41

Talking about your job in general is fine; telling who came in and what they looked like is not.

### Question 42

A password is like a lock on your locker - it keeps other people out of your things.

### Question 43

If you're upset with a teammate, you talk to the coach, not yell about it at the whole school.

### Question 44

It is like a puzzle - even without the name piece, the other pieces can show whose picture it is.

### Question 45

Writing something in permanent marker and erasing it still leaves a faint mark - and others may have taken a photo of it.

### Question 46

You leave a short, safe note on a door, not the whole story anyone walking by could read.

### Question 47

Private mail goes in a sealed, locked envelope, not on a postcard everyone can read.

### Question 48

A club can share general news but not the private details of its members.

### Question 49

When someone writes something mean, you tell a grown-up in charge instead of fighting in the comments.

### Question 50

PHI is like a name tag stuck to someone's health details - together they point to a specific person.

### Question 51

You only take the crayons you need for your picture, not the whole box every time.

### Question 52

A picture of someone in the doctor's office can say who they are - so it is private.

### Question 53

A name is like the label on a folder - it tells you whose private papers are inside.

### Question 54

If you spill something, you tell an adult right away so it can be cleaned up - not hide it.

### Question 55

When something goes wrong, the right move is to tell the person in charge, not just anyone nearby.

### Question 56

It is like having a work desk and a home desk - different things happen at each one.

### Question 57

Privacy settings are like closing your curtains - they help, but you still choose what is in the room.

### Question 58

Official messages go through the office mailbox, not your personal chat.

### Question 59

A signature is like a nametag on your letter - it says who you are and how to reach you.

### Question 60

What you post is like what you wear in public - people form an impression.

### Question 61

An open question is like opening a door wide, while a yes-or-no question is a tiny crack.

### Question 62

If a friend says no thank you to a snack, you don't force it on them - no means no.

### Question 63

Secrets are for private rooms, not busy hallways where anyone can listen.

### Question 64

A speaker is like a loudspeaker at a game - everyone nearby hears it, so use it carefully.

### Question 65

Chest pain is like a fire alarm - you don't guess it's a drill; you get help right away.

### Question 66

You dress up for a special event because it shows respect - work is a place to look neat and professional.

### Question 67

Giving a ride is something a friend does, and the assistant is a professional, not a friend.

### Question 68

If someone keeps poking you and you don't like it, you say stop - and tell an adult if it keeps happening.

### Question 69

A patient's business stays at the office, like a library book that never leaves the building.

### Question 70

Taking a big gift to say nice things about a product is like getting paid to be a friend - it is not honest.

### Question 71

You don't peek at a classmate's test paper just because you are curious about their answers.

### Question 72

You lock your locker before walking away so no one can open it as you.

### Question 73

If you mail a letter to the wrong house, you tell the person in charge, not pretend it never happened.

### Question 74

Questions about your bill go to the office's front desk, not to a friend's chat app.

### Question 75

Moving your work papers to your home backpack without permission is not the same as leaving them in the locked office.

### Question 76

You don't play games on the class computer while the teacher is teaching - it is for classwork.

### Question 77

Two-factor is like needing both a key and a secret knock to get in.

### Question 78

A video call about private health is like a private meeting - the door stays closed.

### Question 79

Identifiers are like the pieces of a nametag that point to one specific person.

### Question 80

A secret is a secret no matter whose it is - staff deserve privacy too.

### Question 81

You don't take pictures of people without their okay, especially somewhere private like a doctor's office.

### Question 82

Telling the whole world where you are every day is like leaving your front door key outside.

### Question 83

Announcing when you will be away is like telling strangers your house will be empty.

### Question 84

Important work papers stay in the locked office cabinet, not your home drawer.

### Question 85

If you are not sure a toy is yours to take, you leave it on the shelf.
